heard: Marine biologists accidentally killed the oldest living animal known to science. In 2006, researchers from Bangor University were dredging the cold sea floor off the northern coast of Iceland. They collected an ordinary ocean quahog clam and immediately froze its solid along with all their other samples. Only after later, slicing the thick shell open in the laboratory, did they discover its astonishing true age. Named Ming by journalists, the unfortunate animal had been quietly alive since 1499 during the Ming Dynasty. Precise carbon-14 dating later proved it had amazingly survived for 507 years. Marine biologists accidentally killed the oldest living animal known to science.
